# China Festivals

> A decision guide to China's festivals, with 2027 dates, a festival finder, best cities, foods, and insider tips for travellers.

China Festivals helps travellers decide which of China's 22 festivals to experience, when to go, and where. It covers lunar festivals (Spring Festival, Mid-Autumn), ethnic festivals (Water Splashing, Torch), modern holidays (Harbin Ice, National Day), and seasonal events (cherry blossoms, Luoyang peonies).

## Pages

- [Home: China Festivals 2027 guide](https://www.festivals-china.com/): 2027 dates, festival finder, all 22 festival guides, city advice, packing lists, visa summary, and FAQ.

## Sections

- [Festival Finder](https://www.festivals-china.com/#finder): choose a festival by traveller type or by month.
- [China festival calendar 2027](https://www.festivals-china.com/#calendar): Gregorian dates with lunar anchors and 2028 previews.
- [All 22 Chinese festivals, explained](https://www.festivals-china.com/#festivals): history, food, venues, itineraries, and tips per festival.
- [Where to experience each festival](https://www.festivals-china.com/#cities): city-by-city festival mapping.
- [Travel tips](https://www.festivals-china.com/#tips): what to pack, eat, where to stay, and getting around.
- [Visa: the short version](https://www.festivals-china.com/#visa): 30-day visa-free entry and the 240-hour transit policy.
- [FAQ](https://www.festivals-china.com/#faq): common questions about dates, crowds, food, and logistics.
- [About this guide](https://www.festivals-china.com/about/): who writes it, editorial standards, and sources.
- [Privacy policy and terms of use](https://www.festivals-china.com/#privacy): data handling and site terms.

## Key facts

- Chinese New Year 2027 falls on February 6, 2027.
- Mid-Autumn Festival 2027 falls on September 15, 2027.
- China offers visa-free entry to citizens of 76 countries, plus a 240-hour transit-free policy for 55 countries.
- Lunar festivals shift dates every year; this guide is refreshed each January.
